subject: CardioSense — privacy follow-up and DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@cardiosense.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CardioSense — privacy follow-up and DPA clarifications

Hi Ava — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment for legal: 

Key asks you raised on the call:
- Controller vs processor mapping for the CardioSense integration (explicit list of which components process PII).
- Subprocessor list and notification commitments (when and how you’ll be notified).
- Breach notification windows and routing (who to contact at CardioSense legal and incident ops).
- Retention windows for request logs, full request/response payloads, and aggregated telemetry.
- Samples of redacted logs / evidence that demonstrate retention and access controls.
- Data residency options (EU/US) and whether we can pin a region for CardioSense test vs prod.

Attached: our current DPA draft (redwood-dpa-v1.1.pdf) — this is the version we generally start from so your legal team can mark up.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Please share the primary legal contact (name + email) we should loop in for redlines.
2) If you can send a single doc with the two highest-priority asks (mapping + breach timeline requirement) we’ll prioritize an answer within 48 hours.
3) We’ll prepare a short controller/processor matrix and sample redacted logs for your review.

Would next Tuesday (4/27) at 10am PT work for a follow-up with your legal and incident ops folks?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-v1.1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ava Patel <ava.patel@cardiosense.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@cardiosense.ai>, legal@cardiosense.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioSense — privacy follow-up and DPA clarifications

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful.

Quick clarifications from our side: 
- Primary legal contact is Samir Rao (samir@cardiosense.ai) — I’ve cc’d him.
- For the mapping, we specifically need to see where PII is processed vs logged (production inference payloads, application logs, analytics telemetry). A single spreadsheet that maps endpoints/components to data types is ideal.
- Breach notification: CardioSense requires vendor notification within 72 hours of vendor confirmation of a probable data breach. If you have a standard notify timeline in the DPA, please highlight it.
- Subprocessor notification: we expect to be notified within 24 hours of vendor identification of an impacted subprocessor, plus access to subprocessor SOC2 reports if available.
- For evidence, we don’t need full logs yet — a redacted sample showing timestamps, request id, and retention TTLs will do.

I’m attaching a short dataflow diagram from our side to help (cardiosense-dataflow.pdf). We’re aiming to close the contract in the next two weeks so speed is appreciated.

Ava
Head of Integrations, CardioSense
ava.patel@cardiosense.ai
[Attachment: cardiosense-dataflow.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks Ava — looping in our privacy and product ops folks to get concrete artifacts. Tessa / Jonas / Laura — please see CardioSense asks above and prioritize the following deliverables: 

1) Controller/Processor mapping spreadsheet (single tab) that highlights: component, data types processed (PII/PHI/non-PII), where data is stored, and region/residency for each component. Deliverable: redwood-controller-processor-mapping.xlsx.

2) Redacted sample logs showing request id, timestamp, and TTL/retention metadata (remove all PII). Deliverable: evidence-playbook.md as a short explanation + one redacted sample.

3) Confirm breach and subprocessor notify timing language we’ll propose in a narrow DPA clause (we typically propose 72 hours for confirmed breaches + 24 hours for subprocessor identification notice; happy to make this configurable for enterprise customers).

Ava — we’ll push the two artifacts above to the Drive link (below) and follow up with a brief call if needed. If CardioSense legal wants to redline the DPA directly we can accept DocuSign or a tracked Word doc — whichever you prefer.

Timeline: aiming to have the mapping + sample logs to you by EOD Monday 4/26.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@cardiosense.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioSense — privacy follow-up and DPA clarifications

Hi Ava / Marissa — following up with the artifacts and short answers. 

Summary answers: 
- Controller vs Processor: Redwood will be processor for inference request handling and transient KV cache; CardioSense is controller for customer data and downstream decisions. We have attached a single-tab mapping that calls out each service component and the data type processed.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessors list in the DPA; per request we can provide SOC2 summary reports for infra subprocessors. We will commit to notifying CardioSense within 24 hours of identifying an impacted subprocessor.
- Breach notice: Redwood’s standard clause proposes notification within 72 hours after confirming a probable data breach; we’ll surface incident triage notes and affected scope as soon as available. If CardioSense requires a shorter SLA, note it in a redline and we’ll evaluate operational feasibility.
- Retention & logs: production request logs are retained for a default of 30 days (configurable on enterprise tiers). Metrics and aggregated telemetry are retained separately; retention TTLs are documented in the attached mapping and the evidence playbook. We will share one redacted request sample via the Drive link below within business day.

Artifacts & links: 
- Controller/processor matrix: redwood-controller-processor-mapping.xlsx (attached)
- Evidence playbook + redacted sample: evidence-playbook.md (attached)
- Secure drive (redacted logs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Ccardio-redwood-evidence
- DocuSign (DPA redline): https://www.docusign.net/Sign?tr=abc123cardiosense

Next steps: if CardioSense legal is comfortable with the 72/24 windows above, sign the DPA and we’ll schedule a production cutover window. If you want a joint call to walk through the mapping, we can do 30 minutes on Tue 4/27 10am PT (Marissa — can you confirm?).

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai
[Attachments: redwood-controller-processor-mapping.xlsx, evidence-playbook.md]
